Court No. - 52
Case :- Writ - C No. - 32516 of 2016
Petitioner :- Jitendra Kumar Pathak

Respondent :- Commissioner Kanpur Division Kanpur And 2 Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Prabal Kumar Dixit,Rajeev Mishra
Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.,Anil Kumar Sharma,Durgesh Kumar Singh,Ekta Kaur,Jagriti
Hon'ble Kshitij Shailendra,J.
1.

This writ petition has been filed challenging the orders impugned dated 11.09.2013, 20.08.2015 and 13.05.2016 respectively passed by the Sub Divisional Magistrate-Etawah (respondent no.3),
District Magistrate/Collector-Etawah (respondent no.2) and Commissioner, Kanpur Division,
Kanpur (respondent no.1).
2.

By the order dated 11.09.2013, the Sub Divisional Officer/ Sub Divisional Magistrate-Etawah has cancelled the Domicile Certificate issued in favour of the petitioner, by the order dated 20.08.2015,
the District Magistrate-Etawah has dismissed the first appeal filed by the petitioner under the Janhit Jitendra Kumar Pathak vs Commissioner Kanpur Division Kanpur ... on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161464812/
1 Gaurantee Adhiniyam-2011 against the rejection order and by the third order dated 13.05.2016, the second appeal filed against the aforesaid orders has also been dismissed by the Commissioner,
Kanpur Division, Kanpur.

sentences.text: 3. The facts, as culled out from the pleadings contained in the writ petition, are that the petitioner being a resident of Village Badhpura District Etawah, since 2009, applied for issuance of a Domicile Certificate on 24.04.2012 in the prescribed form alongwith the Certificate issued by the Village Pradhan.
On the application submitted by the petitioner, a report from the concerned Lekhpal was called and, after due process, a Domicile Certificate was issued in favour of the petitioner on 10.05.2012.

It has been pleaded that petitioner suffered from bullet injury in his backbone on 04.09.2009 resulting in 100% disability restricting his movement which fact was certified by the Chief Medical Officer-Etawah vide his certificate dated 03.06.2010 and the petitioner applied for L.P.G. distributorship pursuant to the process issued for such dealership which was reserved for "physically handicapped persons".
The petitioner was granted the dealership after due process.

4. It is contended that some persons having enmity with the petitioner lodged a complaint with malafide intentions before the Indian Oil Corporation attacking on the eligibility of the petitioner,
however, the same was found to be false in enquiry.

Further complaint was moved by one Pappu, on which, notice was issued to the petitioner which was also replied by him and, thereafter, an enquiry was conducted by Naib Tehsildar concerned who submitted a report dated 04.02.2013 recording that no person named Pappu was residing in the village and that the complaint was manufactured.
It was further reported that the petitioner was a resident of Village Badhpura.

It is also stated that during the course of enquiry, the petitioner submitted various documents like Khasra, Khatauni,
Statement of Bank Accounts, Certificate issued by the Village Pradhan and ration card bearing No.229771 dated 08.12.2012, however, during the course of proceedings, another forged, fabricated and manufactured ration card bearing No.170016 allegedly issued in the name of the petitioner was also inserted/planted on the file.

It is further stated that relying upon the aforesaid forged and fabricated ration card bearing no.170016, the Sub Divisional Officer cancelled the Domicile Certificate vide impugned order dated 11.09.2013 which has been upheld in two subsequent orders passed by the first and second appellate court/authorities, respectively.

5. The specific case of the petitioner in the writ petition is that he had not enclosed a copy of ration card alongwith application form and, therefore, the reason assigned in the orders impugned that petitioner had produced a forged and fabricated ration card alongwith his application form is wholly perverse, untrue and unsustainable.
6.

A counter affidadvit has been filed by the respondent no.5-Keshav Deo in the capacity of a complainant stating that though the petitioner was a physically handicapped person but he was not resident of Village Badhpura, District Etawah.

Further contention in the counter affidavit is that another ration card bearing no.149412 was also issued in the name of the petitioner's father showing the name of the petitoner as his family member and, therefore, the ration card produced by the petitioner for obtaining Domicile Certificate becomes invalid.
It has also been pleaded in the counter affidavit that regarding fictitious ration card bearing no.229771, First Information Report was also lodged against the petitioner.

It is further pleaded that in Sessions Trial No.408 of 2009 (State v.
Jitendra Kumar Pathak vs Commissioner Kanpur Division Kanpur ... on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161464812/
2 Manish Bhadoria & Ors.), the petitioner appeared as a witness and in his statement, he had disclosed his address as that of ''619A, Civil Lines, Police Station-Civil Lines, District Etawah'.
7.

entities.text:
Sessions Trial No.408 of 2009 (State v.
Jitendra Kumar Pathak vs Commissioner Kanpur Division Kanpur
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In sum and substance, the defence taken in the counter affidavit is that the petitioner was a resident of different place other than Village Badhpura and, hence, he had procured the Domicile Certificate by wrongful means and got the L.P.G. distributorship.

8. As regards the First Information Report concerning the alleged procurement of Domicile Certificate, the petitioner has filed a supplementary affidavit stating that he was bailed out in Case Crime No.13 of 2014 which was registered under Sections 419, 420 I.P.C. and the criminal case is pending at the trial stage.

9. A counter affidavit has been filed on behalf of the State-respondents supporting the impugned orders stating that the petitioner was provided full opportunity of hearing before the authorities below who have examined the material on record and have passed the orders impugned which do not call for any interference.
10. The petitioner has filed rejoinder affidavit against the counter affidavits and has reiterated the version contained in the writ petition.

11. I have heard Shri Atul Dayal, learned Senior Advocate assisted by Shri Prabal Kumar Dixit,
learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Standing Counsel for the State-respondent nos.1 to 4 and Ms. Ekta Kaur, learned counsel for the respondent no.5.
I have also perused the record.

12. The dispute in the present writ petition is with regard to validity of the Domicile Certificate issued in favour of the petitioner on 10.05.2012 and the controversy is as to whether the petitioner had procured the said Domicile Certificate by producing a fake ration card showing himself to be resident of Village-Badhpura, District-Etawah.

13. Shri Atul Dayal, learned Senior Counsel, has vehemently argued that when the petitiooner had applied for issuance of Domicile Certificate, his application (Annexure No.1 to the writ petition) did not contain any description or requirement of ration card nor did he submit the same alongwith the application form.
Further contention is that ration card bearing No.229771 was produced by the petitioner during the course of enquiry proceedings and the said ration card was thorougly genuine.

He submits that insofar as another ration card bearing no.170016 is concerned, the same is the document manufactured by the complainant side and was somehow inserted and planted during the course of enquiry.
He has referred to ''Annexure 12' to the writ petition which is a ration card bearing No.170016 allegedly issued on 15.04.2008.
He further submits that the said ration card was never issued on 15.04.2008 or on any other date.

He also submits that forgery committed by the complainant side in the said ration card bearing No.170016 is apparent on the face of the record,
inasmuch as, in the petitioner's photograph pasted on the ration card, he has been shown as a physically handicapped person although in the year 2008, the petitioner was not physically handicapped but he suffered bullet injury in his backbone on 04.09.2009 and he received his medical treatment while residing at his In-laws' address at 619A, Civil Lines, Police Station-Civil Jitendra Kumar Pathak vs Commissioner Kanpur Division Kanpur ... on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161464812/
3 Lines, District-Etawah and the First Information Report concerning the incident dated 04.09.2009 was also lodged showing the same address of the petitioner which has nothing to do with the permanent address of the petitioner i.e. Village Badhpura.
14.

Learned Senior Counsel has drawn attention of the Court towards many other documents to demonstrate that he is resident of Village-Badhpura and has contended that the authorities below,
while passing the orders impugned, have recorded absolutely perverse and wrong findings that the petitioner had, alongwith application form, annexed and submitted ration card bearing No.170016 dated 15.04.2008 whereas the specific and consistent case of the petitioner is that he never produced such ration card at any stage, rather, during the course of enquiry proceedings, the only ration card bearing No.229771, which is genuine, was produced by him.
15.

The contention of learned counsel for the respondent no.5, on the other hand, is that the petitioner has himself shown his address as "619A, Civil Lines, Police Station-Civil Lines, Etawah"
and that the ration card dated 15.04.2008 bearing No.170016 was produced by the petitioner for obtaining Domicile Certificate.
16.
Before dealing with the rival contentions of the parties, it is necessary to refer to the order dated 20.07.2016 passed by this Court in the present writ petition.
The same is quoted hereinbelow:-
"Vakalatnama of Sri Rajiv Misra filed today, is taken on record.
Petitioner is permitted to implead the complainant as respondent no. 5 in the writ petition.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the application for grant of domicile certificate did not accompany any ration card and therefore, his domicile certificate,
could not be cancelled on the ground that such ration card was forged.
Learned Standing Counsel as well as Sri D.K. Singh who appears for respondent no. 5 prays for and are granted a weeks' time to obtain instructions in the matter.
Put up once again as fresh on 27th July, 2016.

Till the next date of listing, no further action would be taken against the petitioner on the basis of the orders under challenge. "
17.

Pursuant to the aforesaid order dated 20.07.2016, learned Standing Counsel produced the original record and after perusing the original records, this Court passed the following order dated 02.08.2016:-
"Supplementary affidavit filed today is taken on record.

Jitendra Kumar Pathak vs Commissioner Kanpur Division Kanpur ... on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161464812/
4

sentences.text: Pursuant to the order passed on the previous occasion, learned Standing Counsel has produced the original records.

Application of the petitioner, which is on record,
shows that the domicile certificate has been claimed by the petitioner on the basis of certificate given by the Gram Pradhan.
In the original application, there is no reference of any ration card.
It is only upon the reverse side of the application that there is some report of Tehsildar, referring to the ration card, which is not the part of the application.
It is thus stated that basis of impugned order is wholly non-existent.
Matter requires consideration.

Learned Standing Counsel appearing for respondent nos.1 to 4 and Sri D.K. Singh,
appearing for respondent no. 4 pray for and are granted 4 weeks time to file counter affidavit.
Rejoinder affidavit may be filed within 2 weeks' thereafter.
List thereafter.

Interim order, granted earlier, will continue till the next date of listing. "
18.
The afore-quoted orders clearly make out that alongwith the application form, no ration card was annexed by the petitioner, nor, was there any requirement for the same.

Therefore, there is nothing on record contrary to the observations made by this Court in the aforesaid orders that the ration card bearing No.170016 or any other ration card was produced by the petitioner at the time of submitting application form for obtaining Domicile Certificate.

19. Surprisingly, the State in its counter affidavit has also relied upon same application form which has been annexed by the petitioner alongwith this writ petition and I do not find any requirement of production of ration card alongwith the application form, therefore, the contents of ''paragraph 16'
of the counter affidavit filed on behalf of the State that the petitioner had filed a copy of the ration card bearing No.170016 dated 15.04.2008 alongwith the application

, becomes unacceptable,
particularly in view of the order dated 02.08.2016 passed by this Court in the present writ petition after perusing the original records.

20. Even otherwise, I find that the petitioner suffered bullet injuries on 04.09.2009, on account of which, he became physical handicapped and, therefore, he was not a ''handicapped person' on 15.04.2008 i.e the date on which ration card bearing No.170016 was issued and, therefore, from looking into the said two dates coupled with the photograph pasted on the said ration card, it is clear that the story set up by the complainant side that the petitioner had obtained Domicile Certificate by producing ration card dated 15.04.2008 becomes unbelievable and contrary to the factual position.
21. Insofar as, ration card bearing No.229771 is concerned, it was issued on 08.12.2012, whereafter,
the L.P.G. distributorship was granted in favour of the petitioner.
I do not find anything contrary to doubt the genuineness of the ration card bearing No.229771, particularly when, during the course of initial enquiry, the same was found to be a genuine document.

sentences.text:
Insofar as, ration card bearing no.149412 issued in the name of petitioner's father is concerned,
there is a report of Village Development Officer dated 26.02.2013 submitted before the Block Development Officer-Badhpura filed as ''Annexure No.3' of the counter affidavit on behalf of respondent no.4; Clause 2 of the said report clearly indicates that units were cancelled in the said ration card and the certificate pertaining thereto was issued on 01.12.2012.
23.

According to the learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner, once the entry made in the name of the petitioner in the ration card issued in his father's name in ancient time was scored out/cancelled and subsequent ration card bearing No.229771 was issued describing the name of the petitioner, his wife and children on 08.12.2012, merely because earlier in the ration card of petitioner's father, the name of the petitioner was there, which was subsequently expunged, the same would not adversely affect the case of the petitioner.

24. I have already dealt with the contention of the complainant side regarding address of Civil Lines shown by the petitioner in the proceedings of some criminal case, however, the stand and explanation of the petitioner to the effect that when he suffered injuries on 04.09.2009, he was medically treated while residing in his In-laws home at Civil Lines Etawah is found to be satisfactory.
The same stand was taken by the petitioner throughout the proceedings of enquiry but it has not been given any consideration in the orders impugned.
25. There is another aspect of the matter.
Admittedly, the L.P.G. distributorship was reserved for physically handicapped persons.
It is not disputed by the respondents that petitioner on the date of grant of distributorship was a person belonging to "physically handcapped category".

During the course of arguments, this Court raised specific queries from all the learned counsel as to whether the respondent no.5-Keshav Deo was an applicant in the dealership, however, the answer came in negative.

Therefore, it is a case where, the complainant side may be having some grudges against the petitioner on account of grant of L.P.G. distributorship and, therefore, time and again complaints were moved not on the merits of the petitioner's claim for distributorship but attacking on the Domicile Certificate, which according to the respondents, was obtained by producing a fabricated ration card.
26.

Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case and material on record, this Court finds that the petitioner did not produce the ration card bearing No.170016 dated 15.04.2008,
rather, there was a single ration card bearing No.229771 issued on 08.12.2012 which was produced by the petitioner during the course of enquiry and the same was found to be genuine.

27. The authorities below have simply relied upon the alleged ration card dated 15.04.2008 and certain reports contrary to the claim of the petitioner, however, the over all facts and circumstances and material on record clearly reflect that the alleged ration card dated 15.04.2008 could not form basis for cancellation of Domicile Certificate of the petitioner.
This Court also finds that the complaints were malicious in nature, particularly when, in earlier round of investigation and enquiry, complaints were found to be false as well as fictitious.

6 28.

sentences.text: In view of the above, the orders impugned which are based upon alleged ration card dated 15.04.2008 as a ground for cancellation of Domicile Certificate, cannot sustain.
29. Accordingly, the writ petition is allowed.

A writ of certiorari is issued quashing the orders impugned dated 11.09.2013, 20.08.2015 and 13.05.2016 respectively passed by the Sub Divisional Magistrate-Etawah (respondent no.3), District Magistrate/Collector-Etawah (respondent no.2) and Commissioner, Kanpur Division, Kanpur (respondent no.1).
No order as to cost.
